record_type_quote: Schnall, Benton, and Harvey (2008; hereafter SBH) conducted two studies and found that participants primed with cleanliness rated moral vignettes as less wrong than participants in control conditions. They propose that feelings of cleanliness induce a sense of moral purity that is misattributed to the moral judgments following the postulates of the mood as information model (Schwarz & Clore, 1983). The goal of the present research is to replicate the results of SBH.

targets.title: With a clean conscience cleanliness reduces the severity of moral judgments
targets.evidence_quote: Schnall, Benton, and Harvey (2008; hereafter SBH) conducted two studies and found that participants primed with cleanliness rated moral vignettes as less wrong than participants in control conditions. They propose that feelings of cleanliness induce a sense of moral purity that is misattributed to the moral judgments following the postulates of the mood as information model (Schwarz & Clore, 1983). targets.outcome_quote: We did not find evidence that physical cleanliness reduced the severity of moral judgments using samples sizes that provided over .99 power to detect the original effect sizes.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Both new-sample experiments failed to support the cleanliness effect; general discussion calls each an informative failure to replicate.
